entries.note: Nakamura 2006 resolves (Cancer Res, PMID 16982756); quote verbatim in the abstract; no HCC patient had been dosed with a member drug by 2006, so the untested opening stands.

entries.rule: decision 4 (engagement: the model's PD readout moved in dosed humans) + decision 15 (readout_tier downstream)
entries.note: McNamara 2015 full text (Wiley): DCE-US tumour blood volume fell at 2 weeks in 8/12 axitinib HCC patients, the model's DCE vascular readout moving as predicted. Downstream same, product_in_model false, comparison_stated false, direction_only, confidence medium (n=12).
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 4 engagement: the model's DCE vascular readout moved in dosed HCC patients (McNamara 2015, 8/12 tumour blood volume fell); decision 15 downstream, decision 11 direction_only, decision 8 proxy (product_in_model false). Same.

entries.note: Quote verbatim in the full text (fc.py scrape). The judgement is wrong that the 2021 tivozanib review states no exposure comparison (it does, intro: rat 0.2 mg/kg Cmax 70-108 ng/mL vs 86.9 ng/mL at 1.34 mg/day), but no human was dosed in 2006, so untested stands.

entries.rule: decision 4 (dose floor, case 2: target reached) + decision 3 (non-HCC patient PK accepted like healthy-volunteer PK; rule question 1)
entries.note: FDA 212904 Multidiscipline Review (tier 2, comparison stated) says the rat-effective exposure (Cmax 70-108 ng/mL, AUC 1640 ng*h/mL) was within the range reached at 1.34 mg/day in solid-tumour patients; the draft says no such comparison exists. Sufficiency in HCC (1 mg RP2D, indeterminate efficacy) stays open.
entries.adjudication_note: RULE QUESTION: the review states the comparison, but in solid-tumour patients at 1.34 mg, not HCC at 1 mg; decision 3 admits volunteers, decision 12 transfers cross-indication only for safety; decision 4 has no row for reached, efficacy indeterminate.

entries.note: Quote verbatim in the full text; SK-HEP-1 confirmed in the 15-line nude-rat panel by the 2021 FDA review (TGI in 11/15 lines at 0.2 and 14/15 at 1 mg/kg/day). The abstract omits hepatic; the full text and the review include it.

entries.rule: decision 4 (efficacy, #32: missed primary + significant secondary is untested unless the source's own conclusion calls it a match; #53: failed means the predicted effect was absent or reversed)
entries.note: Kang 2015 (PMID 26386123, registry results 2015-05-27 confirmed): OS primary missed (HR 0.907) but PFS, TTP and CBR significantly favoured axitinib and the conclusion says so. The xenograft predicted tumour growth inhibition, which was present; under #32 this is untested, not contra.
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 4 (#32): OS primary missed, PFS/TTP/CBR secondaries significant, trial paper draws no model comparison, so untested; #53: the predicted tumour-growth effect was present, not absent, so not contra. Facts undisputed.

entries.rule: decision 4 (efficacy, case 2: primary met as predicted) with decision 6 (#3, one drug's contra overrides another's same) no longer engaged once the axitinib entry is untested
entries.note: AHELP (Qin 2021, PMID 33971141; NCT02329860 results 2024-01-22 confirmed) met its OS primary vs placebo with apatinib in the model (Yang 2018, epub 2018-08-14, before the 2020 readout). With no contra left on the track the 2021 status is same, direction_only; Fountzilas 2020 does not score (#53).
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 4 case 2: AHELP OS primary met with apatinib in the model (Yang 2018, prospective, not retrodiction per decision 10). Decision 6 #3 no longer applies once efficacy 2 is adjudicated untested; same, direction_only.

entries.rule: decision 8 (a model used for the class with no patient comparison is untested, not blank)
entries.note: Staffeldt 2023 resolves (Cells, PMID 38201286, epub 2023-12-30); quote verbatim in the abstract; the four donors were never dosed, so untested on its own patient-derived track is right. A 2024 patient-derived LCSC paper (see missing) belongs on this track.

Nakamura 2006 states phase I was under way (quote verbatim, abstract); the species package was in use but unpublished until the 2012 axitinib and 2021 tivozanib reviews. Untested opening stands; pooling rodent plus non-rodent packages across members is rule question 5.

entries.rule: decision 1 (comparison stated by the source), decision 2 (tier 2), imported_from per safety cell definition
entries.note: Verbatim in the bundled 202324 Pharmacology Review (sources/202324/202324Orig1s000PharmR.txt lines 624-626), reviewer pairs animal BP rise with clinical hypertension. The judgement's 'not observed clinically' paraphrase is not in the text: GI findings are stated to correlate with clinical perforations and bone/teeth are scoped to paediatrics (no decision-5 contra). Status unchanged.

entries.rule: decision 1 (paired by the drafter), safety cell definition
entries.note: Kang 2015 abstract verbatim: hypertension 54% on axitinib in HCC, paired with the 2012 animal cardiovascular findings. Same, direction_only, stands; placebo-arm rate not in the abstract (drafter says so).

entries.rule: safety cell definition; decision 16 placement is rule question 4
entries.note: Qin 2021 verbatim; registry 2024-01-22 confirmed. The tivozanib rat study also showed transient reduced platelet counts (212904 review p.183), so AHELP thrombocytopenia (13% vs 1%) is not a silence miss. Apatinib mouse hypertension (Lu 2019, see missing) would make product_in_model true.

entries.rule: decision 7 (opening at model_first_use_year), decision 8 (own track: immunocompetent syngeneic allograft vs human xenograft in nude rodents)
entries.note: Resolves (Cancer Gene Ther 28:89-97, PMID 32533100, epub 2020-06-12); quote verbatim in the abstract (paywalled; abstract and figure captions read). Fig. 1 caption names Hepa1-6 ('Hep1-6') in C57BL/6: tumour line confirmed syngeneic. Untested opening stands.

entries.rule: decision 4 (efficacy case 2: OS primary met with apatinib in the model), decision 10 (prospective: model received before the first public readout), decision 1 (paired, comparison_stated false)
entries.note: Qin 2021 resolves (PMID 33971141); quote verbatim in abstract. Yang 2020 received 2019-12-28, published 2020-06-12; AHELP first public 2020-05-20 (ASCO), no earlier press release found. Prospective by submission date, as adjudicated efficacy 3; same, direction_only stands.

entries.rule: decision 8 (a model used for the class with no patient comparison is untested, not blank; patient prediction_level), decision 7
entries.note: Full text (PMC11575129) read: quote verbatim in abstract and Results; 12 poor-prognosis LCSC genes cluster TCGA-LIHC; oncoPredict ridge regression on GDSC imputes axitinib among 198 drugs; 16 strains from 24 tissues, 10 tumorigenic; no clone or patient dosed. Untested stands.

entries.rule: A model built or run after the clinic already knew the answer is a retrodiction (retrodiction: true); if it reproduced the human data its status is retro, never same
entries.note: Quote verbatim in Liang 2019 abstract (PMID 31285418, epub 2019-07-08). But hypertension in HCC patients on a member drug was already published (Kang 2015 axitinib 54%, safety entry 3), and apatinib hypertension in gastric-cancer patients by 2016. Retrodiction: retro 2019.

entries.rule: A retrodiction that reproduced the human data is retro, never same
entries.note: AHELP quote verbatim (Qin 2021 abstract, PMID 33971141): grade 3-4 hypertension 28% vs 2%. Pairing is direction-correct, but the Liang 2019 model postdates Kang 2015 HCC hypertension, so the track stays retro; this entry changes no status and could be dropped.

missing: Engagement, HCC patients, member drug: McNamara 2015 (doi:10.1002/cncr.29227, full text) reports DCE-US tumour blood volume decreased at 2 weeks in 8 of 12 axitinib patients and predicted better OS; the draft lists the trial but never scores it against the model's DCE-MRI readout (used for the engagement correction).

Engagement, product in model, other-indication patients: tivozanib first-in-human study AV-951-03-B01 showed dose-dependent decreases in serum sVEGFR-2 and dose-dependent reduction in tumour perfusion (FDA NDA 212904 Multidiscipline Review, sources/212904/212904Orig1s000MultidisciplineR.txt lines 1417-1420; published as Eskens et al. 2011 Clin Cancer Res, DOI not verified here). Scorable only if decision 3 extends healthy-volunteer admissibility to other-indication patients (rule question 1).

Dose, comparison stated: FDA NDA 212904 Multidiscipline Review (intro, ~lines 1121-1126) pairs the rat-effective exposure at 0.2 mg/kg (Cmax 70-108 ng/mL, AUC 1640 ng*h/mL; simulated Css 69.5 ng/mL, p.179) with the clinical exposure at 1.34 mg/day (Cmax 86.9 ng/mL, AUC0-24 1510 ng*h/mL) in solid-tumour patients; the draft states no such comparison exists.

Safety, product in model: Lu et al. 2019, Exp Mol Med (doi:10.1038/s12276-019-0274-7, PMID 31285418) HCC xenograft mice on apatinib developed hypertension and mild liver/kidney damage, a product-in-model safety prediction published before AHELP read out; safety entry 4 could cite it as model_src with product_in_model true.

Patient-level model, no comparison: Journal of Translational Medicine 2024 (doi:10.1186/s12967-024-05870-9, PMID 39558364) patient-derived liver-cancer stem-cell lines; a transcriptomic C2 subtype is predicted sensitive to axitinib, no patient was dosed. Untested entry on the patient-derived track (hcc-patient-derived-primary-cell-lines or its own model_id).

No additional member-drug failure (press release, SEC filing, EMA/AdCom document) for HCC monotherapy was found in the sources reached; title/abstract-restricted Europe PMC searches found no HCC organoid or PDX study of apatinib, axitinib or tivozanib beyond the two above.

Attribution note (models check, CHECKER_BRIEF_v3 / models): the 'Lu 2019' safety item above is Liang Q 2019, Exp Mol Med (doi:10.1038/s12276-019-0274-7, PMID 31285418), on the existing hcc-human-xenograft-immunodeficient-rodent track; the models merge added no safety entry for it, so safety entry 4 still carries product_in_model false.

Models check (safety entries 5-6): no further model system for member-drug HCC safety found; the retro call rests on Kang 2015 (doi:10.1093/annonc/mdv388, axitinib HCC hypertension 54%) and apatinib gastric-cancer phase 3 hypertension (Li 2016 J Clin Oncol, doi:10.1200/JCO.2015.63.5995, not re-opened here) predating Liang 2019.
rule_questions: Decision 3: does PK/PD measured in patients of another indication (tivozanib solid-tumour FIH; RCC dose 1.34 mg/day) count for an HCC dose or engagement cell the way healthy-volunteer data do, when the HCC RP2D (1 mg) was set lower for tolerability and never exposure-matched?

Decision 4 dose table: the model's exposure target was reached (stated by a regulator) but the same drug's efficacy in the context is indeterminate (tivozanib phase 1b/2 stopped without a primary-endpoint verdict, #53 says stopping is not failure). No row covers 'reached, efficacy indeterminate': same on the floor, or untested?

Decision 4 (#32): once the randomised axitinib trial is untested (missed OS primary, significant PFS/TTP secondaries), does the single-arm McNamara 2015 phase 2, whose primary (16-week tumour control 42.3%) was met, score efficacy same for 2015? The draft treats single-arm response primaries as not status-setting.

Decision 16: hypertension was predicted by the class package (mice/rats/dogs; telemetered monkey only at 3 mg/kg, HED 58 mg/day) and appeared at the effective clinical exposure without closing the window (patients dosed to target, hypertension managed). Is that the dose ceiling contra with margin misplaced, or safety same direction_only as drafted? Where is it counted once?

Decision 8 (track identity): is one safety model_id right for the GLP rodent-plus-non-rodent package when members used different species (mouse/rat/dog for axitinib, rat/monkey for tivozanib) and apatinib's own package is unpublished?

Engagement readouts: is a class-standard circulating PD marker (plasma sVEGFR-2 fall, Fountzilas 2020) 'the PD readout the model used' when the model measured tumour-endothelial pVEGFR2 and MVD? The draft kept it untested per a sibling tile; decision 15 defines tiers but not substitutability.

Decision 10 (models check): when a model manuscript was received before the trial's first public readout but revised and published after it (Yang 2020: received 2019-12-28, revised 2020-05-22, published 2020-06-12; AHELP ASCO abstract 2020-05-20), does the submission date or the publication date decide retrodiction? Scored prospective here by submission date, consistent with adjudicated efficacy 3.

Decision 8 (models check): does an in-silico drug-sensitivity imputation (oncoPredict trained on GDSC) that names a member drug among 198 screened compounds, with nothing dosed, count as 'a model used for the class' and open an untested track, or does an in-silico screen need a threshold before it enters the atlas?
